A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Hallo3 and contain readable text, equations, tables, and figures supporting comparison. All 12 pages of v3 and 10 pages of v4 were inspected; neither supplied PDF contains an appendix section.

before.justification: v3 reports original benchmark evaluations, component ablations, guidance-scale experiments, and qualitative text-control comparisons in Tables 1–7 and Figures 6–12.

after.justification: v4 retains original benchmark evaluations and audio-conditioning, identity-conditioning, and motion-frame ablations in Tables 1–6 and accompanying figures.

M1.justification: Both versions retain the CogVideoX backbone, 42-layer identity reference network, audio cross-attention, two-stage training, and extrapolation using two preceding frames. Removed loss documentation and newly disclosed masking details do not establish an actual algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both retain the 134-hour HDTF/YouTube/movie training corpus and evaluations on HDTF, Celeb-V, and the 34-case wild dataset. Nonfrontal portraits, accessories, interactions, and dynamic scenes remain covered. The deleted text-control analyses probe capabilities within this retained task coverage.

E2.justification: SadTalker, DreamTalk, AniPortrait, and Hallo remain the comparators in Tables 1–3. Removing Section 4.4 and Figures 11–12 eliminates the separate qualitative comparisons against CogVideoX, although CogVideoX remains the model backbone and a cited work.

E3.justification: v4 removes the CFG sweep varying text guidance across 1.0/3.5/6.0, audio guidance across 3.5/6.0, and image guidance across 1.0/3.5, together with the matched-prompt CogVideoX comparisons. Retained training budgets, batch size, and tabulated evaluation metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The complete guidance-scale sensitivity study in Table 7 and the subject-interaction and foreground/background text-control analyses in Section 4.4 disappear. This substantially narrows the supplementary analysis, while the audio, identity, and motion-frame ablations remain intact.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or comparable uncertainty estimates for the experimental results.

E6.justification: All numerical results in Tables 1–6 are unchanged. v4 removes the additional CFG results in Table 7, such as Sync-C increasing from 6.154 to 6.469 with higher audio guidance, and the qualitative CogVideoX alignment results in Figures 11–12. These are removed findings, not performance changes in retained comparisons.

T1.justification: The audio-projection expressions, identity encoding and attention relations, and motion-frame padding construction are unchanged. Neither version contains a separate theorem or proof contribution.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about pretrained transformer-based portrait animation, identity preservation, audio conditioning, long-video extrapolation, and dynamic scenes. The revised title and terminology do not redefine the contributions.

C2.justification: v4 removes interpretations connecting audio, text, and image guidance to synchronization, dynamics, and identity consistency. It also drops the specific limitation concerning intricate expressions under varying illumination. The benchmark lip-sync/generalization tradeoff and interpretations of the retained component ablations remain.

D1.justification: v4 removes the exact CogVideoX-5B-I2V initialization, v-prediction loss, MiniCPM caption generation, VBench/RAFT/DINO metric details, and selected CFG settings. It corrects the malformed learning-rate statement to 1e-5 with 480 × 720 resolution, first reports 0.25 motion masking, and replaces H100 training hardware with A100 hardware while adding an eight-A100 experimental server. These substantially alter reproducibility documentation without establishing reruns.

R1.justification: Eleven references disappear, including VBench, DINO, RAFT, MiniCPM-V, the InsightFace toolkit, Tora, and Champ. Most removals concern implementation or evaluation provenance; Section 2 and the central positioning relative to existing portrait-animation and video-generation methods remain essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 revises the title and training-phase prose, abbreviates the experimental discussion, removes Section 4.4 and the limitations/safety paragraphs, and adds acknowledgements. The project URL moves above the abstract. Most remaining prose and the overall section sequence are preserved.

P2.justification: v4 removes Table 7 and both full-width controllability figures, substantially contracting the visual evidence. It also resizes and rearranges retained result displays, including Figures 7–8, and shortens Figure 10 from four displayed frame rows to three with a condensed caption.

improvement.justification: v4 fixes the invalid learning-rate statement and clarifies some training details, but loses guidance sensitivity and text-control evidence, specific limitations, and important reproduction information. These losses weaken support and transparency. Because the central method, claims, and Tables 1–6 remain intact, the net decline is limited.
